"For each item below, fetch its source and check that the recorded quote appears on the page and supports the item. A card item is a field of the plan in the producer's words, with the sources it cites: check each factual claim in it against those sources, and any value it carries against the page; what the plan will build, measure or predict needs no source, but a factual claim with no source is UNSUPPORTED. For a cost input, check that the page states the number for the setting given; whether it applies to this plan is not yours to judge. When the page states a different number for a num or rate item, give it as page_value. Decide only from the pages you fetch and the text below; do not read files. Return one status per item, under its ref: SUPPORTED, PARTIAL, UNSUPPORTED, CONTRADICTED or UNREACHABLE, with the page sentence you relied on.
Items, one per line:
p1:c1: MatterGen is a fine-tunable crystal foundation model, and its released fine-tuned checkpoints cover only chemistry, symmetry, magnetic density, band gap, and bulk modulus — there is no ionic-conductivity or transport-property checkpoint, so the card's conductivity-conditioned adapter is not yet built. | source: https://github.com/microsoft/mattergen | recorded quote: \"We provide checkpoints of an unconditional base version of MatterGen as well as fine-tuned models for these properties: * `mattergen_base`: unconditional base model trained on Alex-MP-20 * `mp_20_base`: unconditional base model trained on MP-20 * `chemical_system`: fine-tuned model conditioned on chemical system * `space_group`: fine-tuned model conditioned on space group * `dft_mag_density`: fine-tuned model conditioned on magnetic density from DFT * `dft_band_gap`: fine-tuned model conditioned on band gap from DFT * `ml_bulk_modulus`: fine-tuned model conditioned on bulk modulus from ML predictor * `dft_mag_density_hhi_score`: fine-tuned model jointly conditioned on magnetic density from DFT and HHI score * `chemical_system_energy_above_hull`: fine-tuned model jointly conditioned on chemical system and energy above hull from DFT\"
p1:c2: Their battery solid-electrolyte discovery today is large-scale screening (32.6M candidates filtered down), not conductivity-conditioned generation, and it ends with synthesis plus a measured conductivity check of the top NaxLi3-xYCl6 candidates. | source: https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2401.04070 | recorded quote: \"By focusing on solid-state electrolytes for battery applications, our discovery pipeline further identified 18 promising candidates with new compositions, and 1 rediscovered a decade's worth of collective knowledge in the field as a byproduct. By employing around one thousand virtual machines (VMs) in the cloud, this process took less than 80 hours.\"
p1:c3: The programme has explicitly stated that the next step beyond screening is direct property-conditioned generation of materials (pointing to MatterGen), which is exactly the step this card targets. | source: https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2401.04070 | recorded quote: \"Future optimization of the workflow beyond screening will be based on the direct generation of materials with given properties, such as the method recently demonstrated by MatterGen [41].\"
p1:c4: The Azure Quantum Elements product leader describes the team's stated ambition as generative battery-materials discovery from property prompts. | source: https://news.microsoft.com/source/features/innovation/how-ai-and-hpc-are-speeding-up-scientific-discovery/ | recorded quote: \"The vision we are working toward is generative materials where I can ask for list of new battery compounds with my desired attributes, Baker says.\"
p1:done: MatterGen has been fine-tuned on magnetic density, band gap, and bulk modulus (never ionic conductivity), and their battery electrolyte result came from screening 32M candidates rather than conductivity-conditioned generation — their own future-tense plan confirms the generative-transport step is not yet done. | source: https://doi.org/10.48550/arxiv.2401.04070 | recorded quote: \"Future optimization of the workflow beyond screening will be based on the direct generation of materials with given properties, such as the method recently demonstrated by MatterGen [41].\"
p2:c1: Their battery workflow uses MatterGen for structure sampling plus MatterSim/DFT screening, and generation is conditioned on thermodynamic stability (convex-hull energy), not on ionic conductivity. | source: https://doi.org/10.1002/batt.202500309 | recorded quote: \"Our LIB material discovery workflow uses MatterGen for structure sampling, [12] MatterSim for initial screening of stable materials, [4] and DFT for final validation.\"
p2:c2: The scale of their generative campaign is tens of thousands of samples (32,600), narrowed to 91 stable Li-containing materials and finally two cathode candidates — so the card's 1k-100k candidate axis sits directly on their scale but targets electrolytes/conductivity, which they did not. | source: https://doi.org/10.1002/batt.202500309 | recorded quote: \"Here, we first conditionally sample structures with a target convex hull energy of 0.03 eV/atom with respect to MP data within the MatterGen framework, and 32,600 structures are generated in this process.\"
p2:c3: Their electrolyte-specific use of a foundation model is property PREDICTION (fine-tuning MACE-MP-0b2-large on a ~400k halide database), not generation — the inverse-design generation they did produced cathodes, leaving conductivity-conditioned electrolyte generation unclaimed. | source: https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/domain-specific-dataset-enable-accurate-mlips-for-disordered-hali/ | recorded quote: \"We demonstrate the utility of the database by fine-tuning the MACE-MP-0b2-large foundation model: the energy root-mean-square error (RMSE) decreased from 154.8 to 10.0 meV atom -1 and the all-force-component RMSE from 168.3 to 39.0 meV Å-1 on a held-out test set, confirming that domain-specific training data is necessary for structurally disordered halide configurations.\"
p2:c4: The generative chapter of their 'inverse design of solid electrolytes' thesis delivers cathode candidates, not conductivity-conditioned electrolytes — confirming the card's step is the unfilled gap in their own programme. | source: https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/deep-generative-models-for-inverse-design-of-solid-electrolytes/ | recorded quote: \"The third contribution moves from screening known materials to inventing new ones. A generative AI model designed for crystals is used to propose tens of thousands of new candidate structures, which are then filtered through a multi-step pipeline combining a universal machine-learning potential and density functional theory. Starting from 32,600 generated structures, the pipeline narrows the field to 91 stable, novel, lithium-containing materials and ultimately identifies two previously unreported candidates that look promising as cathodes.\"
p2:done: They have run MatterGen generation for battery materials (cathodes, conditioned on stability) and fine-tuned foundation models for halide electrolyte property prediction, but have not fine-tuned a generative model on ionic conductivity to generate electrolytes — that exact experiment is absent from both their paper and thesis. | source: https://orbit.dtu.dk/en/publications/deep-generative-models-for-inverse-design-of-solid-electrolytes/ | recorded quote: \"Chapter 5 - Generative Design of Li-Ion Cathodes This chapter reports the generative discovery of cathode materials for lithium-\"

function.name: webfetch
function.description:
- Fetches content from a specified URL
- Takes a URL and optional format as input
- Fetches the URL content, converts to requested format (markdown by default)
- Returns the content in the specified format
- Use this tool when you need to retrieve and analyze web content

Usage notes:
  - IMPORTANT: if another tool is present that offers better web fetching capabilities, is more targeted to the task, or has fewer restrictions, prefer using that tool instead of this one.
  - The URL must be a fully-formed valid URL
  - HTTP URLs will be automatically upgraded to HTTPS
  - Format options: "markdown" (default), "text", or "html"
  - This tool is read-only and does not modify any files
  - Results may be summarized if the content is very large

url.description: The URL to fetch content from

format.description: The format to return the content in (text, markdown, or html). Defaults to markdown.

function.name: websearch
function.description:
- Search the web using the session's web search provider - performs real-time web searches and can scrape content from specific URLs
- Provides up-to-date information for current events and recent data
- Supports configurable result counts and returns the content from the most relevant websites
- Use this tool for accessing information beyond knowledge cutoff
- Searches are performed automatically within a single API call

Usage notes:
  - Supports live crawling modes when available: 'fallback' (backup if cached unavailable) or 'preferred' (prioritize live crawling)
  - Search types when available: 'auto' (balanced), 'fast' (quick results), 'deep' (comprehensive search)
  - Configurable context length for optimal LLM integration
  - Domain filtering and advanced search options available

The current year is 2026. You MUST use this year when searching for recent information or current events
- Example: If the current year is 2026 and the user asks for "latest AI news", search for "AI news 2026", NOT "AI news 2025"

numResults.description: Number of search results to return (default: 8)

livecrawl.description: Live crawl mode - 'fallback': use live crawling as backup if cached content unavailable, 'preferred': prioritize live crawling (default: 'fallback')

type.description: Search type - 'auto': balanced search (default), 'fast': quick results, 'deep': comprehensive search

contextMaxCharacters.description: Maximum characters for context string optimized for LLMs (default: 10000)
